transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Recording: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Avery Chen, Marcus Lee, Priya Nair, Elena Gomez, Noah Park, Lucas Wright
Shared links: (deck) https://redwood.internal/product/q2-launch, (perf sheet) link to spreadsheet, (RCA placeholder) rca/redwood-q2-incident

Summary:
- Quick postmortem of the March 9th production incident that impacted slow start for a small subset of customers; root cause appears related to a kernel selection regression combined with a rolling canary that had relaxed failure thresholds.
- Review of launch readiness items for Q2 feature rollouts; tightened canary criteria, checklist updates, and monitoring additions agreed.
- Action items captured and owners assigned.

Topics:
- Incident timeline / RCA hypothesis
- Kernel selection and quantization path rollback/guarding
- Canary metrics and rollout checklist changes
- Runbook updates and on-call handoffs
- Post-launch monitoring and synthetic benchmarks

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we've got 75 minutes ish on the calendar to go through the incident postmortem and then make sure our q2 launch checklist is updated, Lucas you on mute?
[00:12] Lucas Wright: yeah sorry um, yes i'm here, just want to flag the customer comms note in the deck, we should make it short and sweet
[00:18] Avery Chen: totally, we'll cover comms at the end. Noah can you start with the timeline please?
[00:24] Noah Park: yeah sure, so quick recap, on 03-09 at 02:12 UTC we started seeing elevated latency for ~3% of requests to the hosted API, initial triage pointed at increased tokenization latency but that was a red herring, by 02:25 UTC we saw KV cache misses spike and at 02:30 the per-shard throughput dropped, by 02:45 we had rolled back a recent kernel selection change for one of the newer quantized kernels and that stabilized things.
[01:03] Priya Nair: can i interrupt real quick - the kernel change was merged two days prior right? it was intended to improve long-sequence throughput but we saw bad interactions on the short seq path
[01:15] Noah Park: correct, it was merged 03-07; the problem was the heuristics for kernel selection didn't account for certain batch mix distributions, so for small seqs on certain hardware it picked a slower path, and because the canary didn't fail hard it got promoted.
[01:33] Marcus Lee: yeah the canary thresholds were too lenient, iirc the success rate was 95% for the canary window and that allowed a few outlier errors, should have been 99+ for latency sensitive routes
[01:48] Avery Chen: right, this is the key learning - canary thresholds must be stricter for low-latency routes. Also need automatic rollback when p50 or p95 jumps by >X% - we'll define X in a sec.
[02:05] Elena Gomez: logged customer tickets included specific mention of bursty inference leading to timeouts on dedicated deployments; we should separate dedicated SLA routes from hosted in the rollout policy so dedicated customers aren't affected by hosted experiments.
[02:20] Priya Nair: agree, routing policy needs to be explicit: no experimental kernel selection for Dedicated pools without opt-in. We also should have a config flag to disable new kernel paths per pool.
[02:33] Noah Park: one oddity - some of the logs show mis-tagged hardware labels, ex "nvdiia-a100" transcribed in logs as 'nvdia' in a few places, makes automated rollbacks harder. we've got a bug in the collector that normalizes names.
[02:47] Marcus Lee: hmm that's likely from the node exporter agent parsing, will open a PR to sanitize that.
[02:54] Lucas Wright: small note, in the deck i suggested adding a diagram of the canary flow, like traffic split, metric probes, and automatic rollback hook. visual helps.
[03:05] Avery Chen: agree. Okay technical question - when we rolled back the kernel change, did we also flush KV caches?
[03:12] Noah Park: we didn't initially, that was mistake; the first rollback left stale KV pointers for a short window, which is why a second rolling restart was required around 03:00 UTC. The final stabilization was after both kernel rollback and cache warmup.
[03:30] Priya Nair: so action item - add a pre-rollback cache invalidation step to the rollback playbook. Also add a safety to detect cache pointer mismatches.
[03:41] Marcus Lee: on the perf side, we need to re-run the quantized path benchmarks with a representative short-seq workload; previous benchmarks were long-seq heavy which masked the regression.
[03:55] Avery Chen: good, Marcus and Priya will own the perf retest. Noah will draft the RCA. Elena will handle stakeholder comms. Lucas will update the diagrams and the canary doc.
[04:10] Elena Gomez: on comms - i'd propose two threads: an internal postmortem for sales and support, and a short customer-facing note for impacted tenants; keep language non-technical and link to follow-up for customers with questions.
[04:25] Lucas Wright: note for the checklist: add an explicit 'no kernel promotions during GA windows' rule, and a list of exception approvals.
[04:34] Avery Chen: yes, add the 'GA window' lock. Also, let's formalize the canary thresholds: p50 change < 10%, p95 < 15% for low-latency routes, and automatic rollback if breach persists for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows. We'll iterate but that's the starting point.
[04:58] Priya Nair: that seems reasonable. For dedicated customers we'll require 99.9% success in canary window and a manual sign-off.
[05:10] Noah Park: ops / runbook notes - on-call rotation, first responder should check kernel selector metrics, KV cache miss rate, and the hardware label normalization. Add a dashboard with those three tiles.
[05:28] Marcus Lee: we should also add synthetic traffic tests that simulate the short-seq mix prior to rollout, run them from the same regions as targeted customers.
[05:40] Elena Gomez: timeline for checklist updates? can we have PRs by end of week?
[05:45] Marcus Lee: yes i'll have the perf benchmark PR and checklist PRs by 03-17.
[05:52] Priya Nair: i'll update the rollback playbook by 03-16.
[05:58] Noah Park: RCA draft 03-16, ops dashboard changes 03-18.
[06:05] Avery Chen: ok i'll consolidate and send out the updated deck and the comms drafts by 03-15.
[06:12] Lucas Wright: quick question about monitoring retention - should we increase retention for canary windows? more history helps debugging but costs money.
[06:20] Marcus Lee: maybe set higher retention for canary-related metrics only, not everything; 30 days for canary metrics seems fine. we'll propose options.
[06:30] Avery Chen: sounds good. Any blockers on the action items?
[06:33] Priya Nair: none from eng, just need access to the perf rigs, Marcus will coordinate.
[06:38] Noah Park: ops will need a bit of time to add dashboards, but it's on the list.
[06:43] Elena Gomez: communications approvals - legal wants to vet the customer note, i can loop them in tomorrow.
[06:48] Avery Chen: great. final recap: (1) Noah draft RCA by 03-16, (2) Priya add rollback cache invalidation + playbook updates by 03-16, (3) Marcus run perf and checklist PR by 03-17, (4) Elena draft comms by 03-15 and route to legal, (5) Lucas update canary diagram and docs by 03-15, (6) Ops to add dashboard and synthetic runs by 03-18.
[07:10] Lucas Wright: i'll also add the visual flow to the deck - link will be in the updated deck PR.
[07:18] Marcus Lee: i'll attach the perf spreadsheet and the short-seq workload script in the PR.
[07:24] Priya Nair: quick note - we should add a post-deploy verification step that includes a synthetic KV warmup to avoid cold-start pointer churn.
[07:31] Noah Park: agreed. i'll add that to the runbook too.
[07:38] Avery Chen: ok thanks everyone, i'll send out the updated notes + meeting minutes after i merge these inputs, target EOD 03-15 for the deck + comms draft and follow-up meeting on 03-19 to verify checklist readiness.
[07:50] Elena Gomez: thanks all.
[07:52] Meeting ended.
